Megakernels on a Mac

Should a Metal kernel that prepares the next token’s keys and values also scan the KV cache? An Inkling-inspired decode experiment on an M4 Pro.

Experiments complete · article drafted15 of 16 execution tasks completeView the checklist
ArchitectureBenchmarksChecklist

Inside the two-layer decoder

Follow one token through adjacent local and global layers, modeled on layers 10 and 11 of Inkling 2 Small (zero-indexed). The first layer updates the state that the second layer reads. Each layer has its own convolution histories and KV cache.

What the attention kernel does

For the new token, clip Q and the relative features, convolve then clip K, and convolve then RMS-normalize V without a learned scale. Append K/V at cache precision. Each KV head serves six query heads. Add the learned relative-position term for distances under 1,024, include the token’s zero-value sink in the softmax denominator, then apply the sigmoid output gate.

What we scale

The two-layer stack uses hidden width 1,152, expert width 576, 12 query heads and two KV heads. Head dimension stays 128. Each layer routes to eight of 384 independent softcapped SwiGLU experts. The expert weights across both layers occupy about 2.85 GiB in FP16, excluding router weights, attention weights and working buffers.

Two measurements with different scopes

WorkloadInputs and outputClaim the measurement supports
Global attention at published head dimensionsSeeded projections and state → gated head outputs and updated state. 48 Q heads, 8 KV heads, dimension 128.Latency of the attention path at the checkpoint’s head geometry. At batch one, 4,096 FP16 KV entries take 16 MiB.
Connected two-layer decoderSeeded upstream states → updated block summary. Includes projections, residual mixing, expert routing, all four Conv4s per layer and caches.How the four attention schedules compare once the reduced-width decoder also runs the projections, depth reads and experts.

Seeded weights, incoming states and FP16 storage make this a reproducible execution study. Production Inkling uses trained weights and mixed-precision experts. Model quality, checkpoint generation throughput, training and speculative decoding are outside this benchmark.

Four schedules for one token

Every schedule starts with the same raw projected token features and cache history. It returns the gated attention output, the new K/V entries and the updated Conv4 histories. The full-cache scan reads the exact rounded K/V that future steps will see.

Compiled MLXCompile preparation and gating around fast grouped-query SDPA. Include relative-bias construction. At batch one pass the current per-head sink. For multiple sequences, fold batch into the head axis so each sequence retains its own six-to-one grouping and per-head sink. Verify the chosen execution path in a trace.
Staged MetalEncode preparation, scan and gating in one command buffer. Share math, tiling and work assignment with the single-dispatch version. This isolates the effect of removing boundaries and intermediate writes.
HybridUse custom Metal preparation and Conv4 history updates, then append the rounded K/V via MLX, run tuned attention and apply the gate. Include interop, memory layout changes and synchronization in elapsed time.
Single-dispatch MetalOne threadgroup owns one KV head and its six query heads for one sequence. It prepares K/V, appends one cache slot, streams KV tiles with online softmax and gates the output. Batch one gives eight independent groups at the published geometry.
Why a longer context could change the winner

A single dispatch removes handoffs, but eight groups may leave useful parallelism on the table. At contexts 64 and 4,096, also test a native scan split across context tiles with a second reduction. Compare it at the same precision before attributing a long-context difference to parallelism.

Performance table

Attention medians combine 2 verified sessions, m4pro-02-a, m4pro-02-b. Each attention cell contains 200 paired timing blocks across 2 fixed token states. At 4,096 tokens, dividing the KV scan into chunks reduced median wall time from 2,875 to 432 µs (6.66×).

Each measured cell gives median synchronized wall-clock time in microseconds for one decode step. L is total visible sequence length including the new token, before a local window is applied. A dash indicates an unmeasured cell. The split control runs only at the two batch-one attention endpoints.

Schedule performance by context length

Two-layer precision control

The decoder keeps FP16 expert weights and computes the expert inputs, projections, activation and weighted sum in FP32 using a custom projection kernel. The isolated split-context control was measured only on global attention.

Sessions A and B passed the 15 registered output and state checks against this control’s CPU reference before and after timing. Both lengths have 200 paired blocks.

Measurement contract

Each comparison uses the same precision policy across its four attention schedules. The connected control keeps expert weights in FP16 and performs expert arithmetic in FP32. Generate test inputs and initialize caches outside the timed region. Restore identical starting states for fixed-length trials, rotate representative seeded tokens and routes, warm each compiled shape, and collect at least 100 synchronized samples per reported cell. Measure host-to-completion consistently, tracing representative native GPU intervals separately. Record software revisions, power mode and thermal conditions. Report fallbacks, failures and unstable cells alongside the winners.

Verified on CPU

At 48 Q heads, 8 KV heads and 128 channels per head, the 64-token CPU trajectory matched the independent prefix calculation within 0.00097656 maximum absolute output error. The connected decoder ran at width 1,152. Both layers routed to eight of 384 experts, with 15 finite output and state arrays.

Attention implementations

✓Build the compiled MLX baselineComplete

Use optimized GQA and an additive relative bias. Test batch-to-head sink equivalence against a dense reference, include mask construction and cache updates, and confirm the fast path or label the fallback.

The compiled MLX attention schedule passed both endpoint checks. Its trace resolves one compute encoder. The internal SDPA shader and dispatch count remain unverified.

✓Build staged MetalComplete

Implement preparation, KV scan and gate with a common native math core and preallocated buffers. Encode into one ordered command buffer and verify intermediate and final state.

Output, updated K/V and convolution histories passed the CPU comparison before and after timed runs at both endpoint lengths.

✓Build the single-dispatch Metal kernelComplete

Give each sequence/KV-head pair exclusive write ownership. Stage only live tiles, use online softmax and record compiled resource limits. Require parity with the staged path.

Output, updated K/V and convolution histories passed the CPU comparison before and after timed runs at both endpoint lengths.

✓Build the hybrid scheduleComplete

Combine native preparation with tuned MLX attention and gating in the same calling context. Verify ownership and dependencies and charge any interop copies, layout changes and synchronization.

Output, updated K/V and convolution histories passed the CPU comparison before and after timed runs at both endpoint lengths.

✓Check the parallelism explanationComplete

Implement a native split-context scan and numerically stable merge. Count the sink and current token once. Test 64 and 4,096 positions and capture traces for the matched and split variants.

The split scan exposes more parallel work at long context. Reviewed four marked traces plus native command-buffer timings. The trace granularity leaves achieved occupancy unresolved.
